intended_object: The finite set {I ⊆ 𝓞_K nonzero integral ideal : N(I) = n} of nonzero ideals of the ring of integers of a number field K with absolute norm n, i.e. the fibre of the absolute norm over n (from the docstring and module doc).
explanation:
The definition turns the set `{I : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰ | absNorm I = n}` into a `Finset`, using the finiteness proof `finite_normFiber`. By `mem_normFiber`, an ideal `I` belongs to `normFiber K n` exactly when `absNorm I = n`, which is the intended fibre. The edge cases come out right: the fibre over 0 is empty, because nonzero ideals have nonzero norm, and the fibre over 1 is {1}.

**Generality.** The same construction would work for any Dedekind domain that is free and finite over ℤ, which are the hypotheses of Mathlib's `Ideal.finite_setOfPred_absNorm_eq`. Even so, the number-field setting is the standard one for this object. It is the setting of the Dedekind zeta function and of ideal Dirichlet series, and the rest of the library (`IdealArithmeticFunction K`, `normCoeff`) is built on it. Mathlib's own Dedekind zeta file also works with `𝓞 K`.

**Mathlib counterpart.** Mathlib has no named `Finset` for this fibre. It only has the finiteness lemma, which this definition uses. So this is a thin, correct wrapper at the appropriate generality.
